decisions.issues: v02 is clean. It is a wide storm-grey beach with black rock outcrops and timber in the surf. Nagoji lies small and face down in the foam with his arms flung out and bandaged wrists, and a frayed rope end trails from him, which matches 1.2. There are no irons, chain or collar, and plenty of empty sky for the caption. v01 is not acceptable. It crops Nagoji large in the foreground rather than small in the foam, which breaks the wide establishing beat. It also leaves his hands and wrists unbandaged, which contradicts the bandaged fingers in 1.2.

Minor issues only. The framing is a medium shot with his face included rather than a tight ground-level shot of the hands, and the palms are pressed down, so the raw heels of the palms do not show. Otherwise the beat is correct: bandaged fingers dug into coarse grit, slipping wrist bandages and a sand-crusted left forearm with no mark. The rope loops sit across the chest under the armpits, clear of the neck, with the frayed end in the foam. There is a reddish chafe ring at the ankle, no irons, a moustache, a gold ear stud and an ochre tunic with a cream dhoti. The caption has room in the sky at top right. v02 has the cleaner chin. v01 is the same image with slightly heavier stubble, which is still within 'light stubble at most', so it is the backup.

This is a clean close-up. His cheek is on wet sand, one eye is half open behind wet curls, and he has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a gold ear stud. Foam washes over his shoulder and back, and the left arm is out of frame. The sea and sky at top left leave room for the caption. v01 is identical but shows a heavier stubble and sand-speckle shadow on the chin, still within 'faint stubble at most', so it is the backup.

In v01 the lower legs run up to about knee height at the top edge, behind where the balloons sit. Nothing else of the men shows. The light shifts to a low sun breaking under grey storm cloud, which still sits well beside the grey sky of 2.1. Otherwise it matches the beat: the same low angle along the sand, a moved tide line, and three pairs of bare brown feet walking in from the right edge and leaving a trail of prints. Toe counts and anatomy are sound, and the open sky at left and centre takes the caption and the off-panel voices. Rejected: v02 has only five feet, and the legs are cut off by a hard horizontal line under the balloon. v03 has five disembodied feet ending at the ankle in mid-air. v04 shows only two pairs of legs. v06 shows four feet stacked in a column with no legs. v05 is the backup: three sound pairs of feet, but they stand still in the shallows rather than approaching with a trail of prints, and there is no horizon or sky to show the time shift.

Minor only: the Young Fisherman is drawn upside down (he leans in from behind Nagoji's head), which fits the flat-on-back POV but makes his face slightly harder to read; his faded blue vest shows a little although the script keeps costume for 2.4, and it matches the 2.4 costume. Leader (short grizzled beard, white teeth, cloth on his left shoulder) and Wary Fisherman (long grey-streaked beard, net coil, looking away) match. No text, clean grey sky at centre-bottom for the caption.

Minor: the Fisherman's white cloth drapes over his near (right) shoulder rather than the left named for 2.1 and 2.4; the script for 2.2 does not fix a side. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and gold ear stud, and he flinches with a bandaged hand half raised. The rope loops are across his chest, his left forearm is out of frame, and the fisherman's rough fingers push his hair back. The stormy beach and grey sky match page 1. No painted balloons or text. The sky at top right (above the rocks) takes the Fisherman balloon, and the top-left sky or the low-detail dhoti cloth at bottom left takes the caption.

v02 is acceptable. Water pours from a clay pot into Nagoji's mouth and runs down his clean-shaven chin. His moustache and gold stud match the sheet, rope burns show on his chest, and the background is empty surf. A fisherman's brown arm and cream vest are visible, and the second hand under the pot is plausible. The framing is a medium close-up rather than truly tight, and the pot pours at his lips rather than being pressed to them. That is acceptable. No rope is visible on the chest, which fits because 2.4 shows the rope already cut away. Rejected v01: Portuguese soldiers in morions stand in the background with a fort, the pot is held by a man in a European doublet and belt (the beat is 'They were not Portuguese'), and the brand is shown on his forearm too early.

v02 and v03 are essentially the same image, with pixel differences of under 1 percent. All three fishermen stand at full figure in the scripted costumes. The Fisherman wears a madder-red lungi and a cream vest, with the white cloth on his LEFT shoulder. The Young Fisherman wears an indigo lungi, a blue vest and a headband, and is sheathing a short knife at his waist-knot. The Wary Fisherman wears an off-white lungi and a dark brown vest, with a coiled net and clay floats. The cut rope loops lie on the sand, the broken ship's boat is at right, the black high-sided wreck with a carved stern and broken masts is on the reef, and palms and black rocks fill the shore. The caption area in the sky is clear. Caveats: the Fisherman's beard reads as a moustache with grizzled stubble, lighter than in 2.2. The foreground forearm is probably Nagoji's right, not the scripted left, but it lies outer side up with a sand crust and no readable mark, so the brand stays hidden as intended. Rejected v01: Nagoji's hand has no bandage.

v01 is clean. It is a narrow surf-line strip of foam, floating planks and a torn scrap of sail on a spar, with black rocks at right matching the rest of the page. No human figure appears anywhere, and two clear sky areas take the two captions. Rejected v02: the bottom third of the frame is a blank white area, so the image is broken.

v07 is acceptable, with minor continuity drift. (1) The sky is sunny blue with white clouds, while page 2 and the 3.3 pick have a flat grey storm sky. A sky-only edit to grey overcast would tidy the page but is not required. (2) Both lungis are checked rather than the plain dyed cloth of 2.4. (3) Nagoji's left foot has a bandage wrapped over the toes, which the script does not call for. The anatomy is sound. Everything else matches the beat. Nagoji is at centre with the torn ochre tunic open over red rope-burn lines, a cream dhoti and no rope. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with at most a stubble shadow, and the small gold stud. The Young Fisherman kneels at viewer left (headband, thin beard, blue vest, indigo lungi) and cradles Nagoji's right hand palm up, fingers wrapped and heel bare. The Fisherman kneels at viewer right (grizzled beard, grey-streaked curls, cream vest, white cloth on his own LEFT shoulder, red lungi). He supports Nagoji's left wrist and thumbs sand off the inner forearm above the slipping bandage, where only a faint unreadable smudge shows. The two painted boxes sit in open sky, clear of faces. v08 is a near-identical re-edit of v07. v09 is an acceptable backup, but its full-width boxes crowd the top and the figures are smaller. Rejected: v01 is set in a stone dungeon and the Fisherman wears a red turban. v02 has a fort behind the beach and a bare-chested Young Fisherman whose own arm ends in the bandaged hand. v03 has the same wrong hand ownership (the Young Fisherman holds up his own bandaged hand), his vest is missing, and Nagoji's left fingers are unbandaged. v04 has the Fisherman in a red vest, letter-like strokes on the forearm scar and Nagoji's left fingers unbandaged.

v03 is a clean, tight insert with minor flaws: the blurred background is bright and sunny rather than overcast, and the brand sits fairly close to the wrist bandage. It shows the inner LEFT forearm (the arm enters from viewer right, elbow crease at top) with a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges. It fits the bible's burned marks blurred past reading, with no letters, numerals or cross. The Fisherman's sandy thumb presses in at the left edge, wet sand is scraped around the mark and the soaked bandage edge sits below. It has no painted reserves, which is correct for a no-text panel. v05 is acceptable as backup, but its mark reads as a bumpy blob more than a row of ridges. Rejected: v01's reddish vertical strokes verge on pseudo-letters. v06 shows Nagoji's fingers unbandaged and a rash-like blob.

Acceptable with minor drift. The Wary Fisherman's face does not match 2.4 and 3.4: he has a short grey-and-black beard and short curly black hair, where 2.4 and 3.4 give him a long grey-streaked beard and longer grey-streaked hair. He is also more muscular than gaunt. He stands shin-deep in the wash rather than ankle-deep, and the wreck reads as brown timber rather than the black high-sided hull. What matches: the dark brown vest, off-white lungi and coiled net on his shoulder, alone at the tide line with an uneasy sideways glance up the coast toward the wreck, under the flat grey storm sky of page 2, with black rocks and a palm headland. There are no painted boxes, no text, and his hands are sound. The huge open sky above and to both sides of his head easily holds the caption and both balloons.

Acceptable with minor continuity drift. (1) The brand on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is a darkish, looping, tattoo-like smudge on the visible upper side of the mid-forearm, not the pale puckered patch on the inner forearm shown in 3.2. It is unreadable, with no letters, numerals or cross, and it is small at reading size. A retouch to lighten it into a pale ridged scar would tidy it. (2) The bandages wrap Nagoji's wrists and the backs of his hands, leaving the fingers bare, the reverse of 3.1's finger wraps. This is close to 3.5's treatment. (3) Light stubble shadow on the chin, within the bible's allowance. The beat is right: the Fisherman (grizzled beard, grey-streaked curls, bare head, cream vest, white cloth on his own LEFT shoulder, madder-red lungi) crouches at Nagoji's side. He has turned his head and his open-palmed haggling hand toward the Wary Fisherman, who stands small and apart at the tide line in the left background in the 2.4 costume, with the long grey beard. Nagoji listens with thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic open over rope burns and cream dhoti, with no rope or irons. Flat grey overcast, black rocks, surf and the broken ship's boat. Hands and anatomy are sound, and there is no text. The open grey sky across the top band and between the Wary Fisherman and the Fisherman holds the three balloons clear of faces.

Acceptable with minor drift. (1) The Fisherman's white cloth sits on his near (RIGHT) shoulder, where 2.4 and 3.4 put it on his LEFT. Because he faces the other way from 3.4, this is barely noticeable. (2) The top-left background is a blocky grey stone outcrop, and the foreground has wooden barrels bound with rope. These read as jointed coastal rock and cargo washed up from the wreck, not a fort, but the shot is less of an open beach than 3.4. (3) Nagoji's hand bandages carry faint brownish grime stains; this reads as dirt, not fresh blood. The beat is right: the Fisherman leans in close at left with a hand at his chin, doing sums (grizzled grey beard, grey-streaked curls, bare head, cream vest, red lungi). Nagoji at right meets his eyes: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only light stubble, small gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic open over rope burns, cream dhoti. His hands and wrists are wrapped in soaked, slipping bandages with the fingertips bare, which matches 3.4. The only forearm mark is a faint unreadable mottled patch. The sky is flat grey overcast with broken wreck timbers in the surf. There is no text, the hands are sound, and there are no painted balloons. Open sky across the top band and in the gap between the two heads holds the off-panel Wary line (tail out through the left edge, toward where he stood in 3.4) and the Fisherman's two lines, clear of both faces.

Minor: the Wary Fisherman is a few paces off but his head turns back toward the group, not toward the palms. The brand patch on Nagoji's left forearm is faint and sits on the visible upper side of the arm (not letters, not a cross). The wreck is a skeletal hull close inshore rather than the high-sided black ship on the reef. Nagoji's hands are unbandaged. Otherwise clean: correct costumes for all three fishermen, clean-shaven chin, moustache and ear stud on Nagoji, no restraints, no text, sound hands, and open overcast sky in the upper centre for the balloon. v03 is near-identical but has a more prominent forearm patch and a little less open sky.

The Fisherman points south with his arm instead of jerking his chin, which reads as the same beat. There are fishing huts and boats along the shore in the distance. Nagoji is seen only from behind at the left edge: light jaw stubble (allowed), gold stud, ochre rags. Costume is correct: cream vest, red lungi, white cloth on his LEFT shoulder, grizzled beard. The hazy sky and palms fading down the coast suit the script and bridge to panel 1 better than v04's saturated blue sky. There is wide open sky on the right for three balloons.

Nagoji sits with one knee raised and his arm resting on it, not propped on one elbow as in 4.1 and 4.4. All three candidates share this pose. The brand, pale ridges blurred past reading with no letters and no cross, shows on the upper side of the left forearm rather than clearly on the inner side. The sunny light is brighter than panel 1's overcast. Face matches the sheet: clean-shaven chin, curled moustache, gold stud. There is large clear sky upper right for the caption and speech. The v03 backup wraps his left wrist and one finger in bandage, which the unbandaged panels 1 and 4 do not have. v01 is set in a dungeon with a chain and is rejected.

Minor only. Nagoji is propped on both forearms and hands rather than strictly on one elbow, but his chin is lifted and his shoulders are squared, so the beat reads. The Fisherman's raised brows are subtle. Everything else is clean. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with only stubble shadow and the small gold stud. The brand on his LEFT forearm is a blurred puckered patch with no letters and no cross. He wears no irons. Hands are sound. The Fisherman matches 4.1 and 4.2: grey curls and beard, white vest, shoulder cloth, red lungi. The wreck, beach and weather are consistent. Wide open sky across the top leaves room for all three balloons without covering either face.

Minor only. (1) Nagoji's dangling near arm (his RIGHT) has a small reddish scraped patch mid-forearm. It reads as a fresh sea or rock abrasion, not the puckered brand, but an attentive reader might take it for the brand on the wrong arm. It is small at page scale. (2) The party walks right along the waterline toward the wreck, with the palms and huts behind them on the left. In 4.1 the Wary Fisherman turned toward palms on the right. This is a mild direction flip, not a script violation. The beat is otherwise complete. The grinning Fisherman (red lungi, white vest, shoulder cloth) holds Nagoji's shoulders from behind. The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi and vest, headband) holds his legs under the knee and the ankle. The Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, brown vest, net, same as in 4.1) walks ahead scanning the shore, and a sand crab sidles in the foreground. Nagoji has the moustache, a clean-shaven chin with stubble shadow at most and the gold stud. He wears no irons, manacles, chain or collar. Hands and feet are sound, and there is no text. Clear sky at the top centre, between the Fisherman's head and the Young Fisherman's head, holds both balloons above all faces.

Minor only. The Wary Fisherman (net, off-white lungi) leads but also grips Nagoji's feet, and the Young Fisherman supports him under the thighs from behind, so the carry is shared three ways rather than strictly shoulders and legs. The fishermen wear sleeveless vests, which matches the page 4 art. Nagoji matches his sheet: curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, bandaged hands, no irons. The wreck sits on its reef with the ship's boat untouched on the sand. There is no painted text. Both captions fit over the top-left foliage or the upper-right sea.

Minor only. The Wary Fisherman is not shown, which the script does not require. Some background roofs look tiled rather than thatched. The foreground girls wear short-sleeved tops. The girl's mouth is behind her hand, so her tail goes to the hand at her mouth. Nagoji is on model (curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud) and is carried wet between the two fishermen in the middle distance. The balloon fits over the laterite wall at top left or the sky at top centre.

Minor. The girl in the far-left doorway is small and peeks from behind the door frame rather than clearly shrinking back. Her clothes (beige top, rust skirt) differ from the foreground girl in 5.2 (red top, cream cloth). The Young Fisherman's sharp head turn toward her reads clearly. Nagoji is on model, and the village setting matches 5.2. Both balloons fit in the open sky at top centre.

Acceptable, with notes. The brand on Nagoji's LEFT inner forearm (correct arm, facing camera) is a crisp raised-ridge scrolled monogram that suggests letterforms. It is not legible at any zoom, but it is sharper than the bible's 'blurred past reading'. The Woman stands just in front of the doorway rather than stepping out of it, and her red lips read slightly like lipstick rather than betel stain. The rope burns are raw red welts with no blood. She wipes her hands on her cloth and looks down at his arm. The Fisherman gestures and talks. Nagoji is on model: curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. Both balloons fit in the sky at top left or over the thatch above her.

Minor. The brand is not visible because the forearm is turned palm-down while the Woman washes his cloth-wrapped hand. That hides the fingers as the script asks, but it also hides the brand. The skin carries a faint crackle texture. All script beats are present: dim interior, hearth smoke rising into the roof-hole light, the tunic set aside on the mat, rope burns, clay basin, her grim tight-mouthed face, and the Fisherman squatting at the mat's edge. Nagoji is on model. Balloons fit over the upper-left wall and the upper-centre roof area.

Minor issues only. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, loose curly hair, bare-chested with rope burns, as in 5.5. The Woman wrings the cloth into the basin and the Fisherman (red lungi, cream vest, cloth on his left shoulder) relays with a faint smile. Both forearms are bandaged, so the brand is hidden here, and one set of unbandaged fingers shows briefly at the lower hand; neither is a problem in this panel. The small, soft-focus hanging lamp at the upper right could read as a glass-chimney lamp. The letterer should put one FISHERMAN balloon over that upper-right area (above Nagoji's head, clear of faces), which also hides the lamp, and the other over the wall above the Woman's head at top left.

Minor only. The boy is right: in the doorway, bare-chested with a towel on one shoulder, panting, one hand on the frame, backlit by grey light. The lamp is an open-wick lamp with no glass, the Fisherman (grizzled beard, red lungi, cloth on his LEFT shoulder) and the Young Fisherman (headband, indigo lungi) match, hands are sound, and there is no text. The plain dark upper wall has room for the boy's balloon (tail down-left to his mouth) and the caption. Deviations: the Fisherman looks at the boy rather than exchanging a look. The Young Fisherman's eyeline to the left passes through the Fisherman's face, so it reads as only half an exchange. Rain falls outside over paddy and the floor inside the door is puddled, which the script does not ask for. It also differs from the dry, sunlit doorways in the current 6.4 and 6.5 candidates, so those regenerations should use overcast grey daylight.

v03 is acceptable, with minor notes. The Fisherman (red lungi, grizzled beard, cream vest) crouches by the mat. His right hand crosses his chest to adjust the white cloth on his own LEFT shoulder, and his hands are sound; he looks down, speaking low. Nagoji half-sits on the mat looking up at him. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean chin and the gold stud. The rope burns are reddish welts, not blood. No brand is visible and there are no irons. There are only the two of them, and there is no painted text. Minor points: (1) Through the doorway at the right, a stormy sea, a beached boat and a small hilltop fort show under grey daylight. None of this is in the script; the grey doorway light is fine, but the sea view sits oddly with an inland house. (2) The left painted balloon's tail points down at Nagoji, about 5% of frame height below the balloon body, tip near x=0.21, y=0.19, but both balloon lines are the Fisherman's. The drawn balloon must be sized to cover it. (3) The wrists are bandaged, matching the 6.1 pick. v01 is rejected: it adds the Wary Fisherman (long grey beard) and the Young Fisherman in the background, and the brand on Nagoji's left forearm shows letter-like shapes.

v06 gets most of the beat right: Nagoji is bare-chested on the mat, eyes closed, lit by the hearth, with a clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache and gold ear stud. The two fishermen are softened in the background, turning toward the door, and the upper wall is clear for captions. But at the right edge a person stands in and beyond the doorway: a figure in a dark coat and a brimmed hat or cap, holding a dark blade or stick. The script shows only a broad shadow. The figure reads as an armed European or soldier arriving, and it contradicts the kapitan's look in the very next panel (white turban, pale vest, white mundu, no coat). Also, his hands rest palm-down, so the ridged brand shows on the outer (back) surface of the left forearm, not the inner side the bible requires. The bare fingers are shown directly. The doorway shows a sunlit beach instead of grey daylight.
decisions.correction: Keep v06's composition exactly: Nagoji bare-chested and cross-legged on the woven mat in the left foreground, eyes closed, face tilted up in warm light from the laterite hearth at far left. Keep his thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with no beard, small gold ear stud and long loose curly hair, and the rope burns on his chest. Keep the Fisherman (red lungi, cream vest, white cloth on his LEFT shoulder, grizzled beard, no headband) and the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, faded blue vest, cloth headband) soft and out of focus in the middle ground, straightening and turning their heads toward the doorway at right. Keep the plain dark upper wall clear for two captions. Change: NO person is visible anywhere in or beyond the doorway. No figure, arm, hat, coat, stick or weapon at the right edge or outside. The arrival is shown ONLY by one broad, soft-edged shadow of a stocky, broad-shouldered man with a rounded turban. The shadow is cast from the doorway across the swept earth floor toward the mat. The doorway itself shows only flat grey overcast daylight, with palms and wet ground outside: no sunshine, blue sky or sunlit beach. Clean linen bandages wrap both hands (palms and fingers) and both wrists, so no bare fingers show. The backs and outer surfaces of both forearms are unmarked skin: the brand sits only on the INNER side of the left forearm, so with his hands resting palm-down in his lap it is hidden in this panel.

decisions.issues: v07 stages the core beat well. The kapitan stands centre with his left cheek to camera, the thin scar running from his left ear to his jaw. He has a white turban, grey-flecked beard, pale buttoned vest with flap pockets and white mundu, and looks down at Nagoji. Nagoji looks straight back, eyes open, with a clean-shaven chin, moustache and ear stud; his left forearm is turned inner side up toward the kapitan, showing pale, illegible ridges. There is no text, and the upper-left wall is clear for three captions. But it breaks continuity on the page. Nagoji wears the torn ochre tunic again, although he is bare-chested in 5.5, 6.1, 6.3 and 6.4 (the previous 6.4 correction states he is bare-chested here too), and his bare fingers are shown directly. The Fisherman (red lungi) now wears the Young Fisherman's headband and has a dark full beard instead of his grizzled one, so the two fishermen blur together. Both fishermen stand well back by the door, so the scale beat (kapitan shorter and broader, Young Fisherman just behind him and half a head taller) is lost. A teal garment edge shows under the kapitan's shoulder cloth, hinting at the chapter 6 coat. The doorway shows a sunny blue sky and sea instead of grey daylight.
decisions.correction: Keep v07's composition: low camera at mat level; Nagoji half-reclining against rolled mats in the left foreground, head turned to his left to look straight up at the kapitan, eyes open and steady. Keep his thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with no beard, small gold ear stud and long loose curly hair. His LEFT forearm stays extended toward the kapitan, inner side up, with the pale raised ridges a hand's width above the wrist. Keep the kapitan in the centre, looking down at Nagoji with his own left cheek to camera and the thin scar from his left ear to his jaw lit by the hearth. Keep his white turban, short grey-flecked beard, pale buttoned vest with flap pockets, white mundu and blue-striped white shoulder cloth. Keep the glowing hearth behind and the plain upper-left wall clear for the captions. Change: Nagoji is bare-chested, as in 6.1, 6.3 and 6.4. The salt-stiff ochre tunic was peeled off earlier: draw NO tunic or shirt on him, only the cream dhoti, with raw rope burns across his bare chest. Clean linen bandages wrap both hands (palms and fingers) and wrists, leaving the forearms bare, so the brand still shows. The kapitan wears no teal, blue or dark garment anywhere: the pale vest over a white shirt and mundu is his only outer layer, with no coat or lapel under the shoulder cloth. The Fisherman (red lungi, cream vest, white cloth on his LEFT shoulder) has a short grizzled grey beard and bare, grizzled curly hair with NO headband; only the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, blue vest) wears a cloth headband. Bring the Young Fisherman up to stand just behind the kapitan's shoulder, visibly half a head taller than him, drawing back a half step with the Fisherman beside him, so the kapitan reads shorter and broader than both. The doorway shows only flat grey overcast daylight that rims the kapitan's shoulders: no blue sky, sunshine or sunlit sea.
